# Build prompt — SoundWave-style “Heaven for Producers”

**Goal:** Build a responsive React + Tailwind CSS website (production-ready) that functions like an ecommerce store but where *all content is free*. It uses **Hygraph (GraphCMS)** as the GraphQL backend to manage content (sample packs, presets, plugins, tutorials, comments, contact messages). Tutorials embed YouTube videos. Include an admin “Manage Content” entry that links to the Hygraph admin UI or a protected admin panel. UI and colors should match the provided images: dark navy background, teal/cyan accent, glass panels, pill filters, cards with cover art, large hero with CTA, centered modal for pack details and comment box. Provide code examples for Apollo Client usage, GraphQL queries/mutations, and sample Tailwind config.

---

## High-level requirements (deliverables)

1. React app (create-react-app or Next.js recommended for SEO; Next.js optional).
2. Tailwind CSS for styling. Custom theme tokens matching images.
3. Apollo Client (or urql) for GraphQL calls to Hygraph.
4. Hygraph project with content models and user perms (schema below).
5. Pages & routes:

   * `/` Home (hero, search, quick filters, featured packs)
   * `/packs` All sample packs with genre filters & search + pagination
   * `/packs/[slug]` Pack detail (modal-style overlay or dedicated page)
   * `/presets` Presets listing and details (similar to packs)
   * `/plugins` Plugins listing
   * `/tutorials` Tutorial index (embedded YouTube video grid)
   * `/contact` Contact form
   * `/manage` Manage Content button → Hygraph admin UI or custom admin UI (protected)
6. Comments stored in Hygraph (no-sign-in required). Include spam protections suggestions.
7. Download links open in new tab (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`).
8. Mobile-first responsive layout with accessible semantics.
9. Optional features: audio preview (stream), lazy-loading images, optimistic UI for comments, modals, analytics.

---

## Visual / UX spec (derived from images)

* Global theme: Very dark navy background (`#071425` / `#0b1622`), deep panel color (`#14202a`), gradient hero overlay from `#071425` → `#0b2b38`. Accent teal/cyan for CTA and pills `#00c4d6` → `#00b1cb`. Light text mostly `#e6f6fb` and muted text `#98a7b2`.
* Hero: Large bold headline with two-tone (white + cyan) words, small subheading, centered CTA (rounded pill).
* Top nav: brand left (“SoundWave” with teal highlight), nav links center/right: `Sample Packs`, `Presets`, `Plugins`, `Tutorials`, `Contact`, `Manage Content` (accent button).
* Filters: pill-shaped toggles under hero showing genres (All, lofi, hip-hop, jazz, dance, trap, ambient...). Clicking a genre navigates to the genre page.
* Cards: large square cover art, pack title, creator, genre pills, left aligned CTA “Download” in cyan. Cards show subtle elevation and inner panel dark gradient.
* Modal pack detail: centered card overlay with blurred background, left big cover preview, right metadata, comments input, large “Download Now” CTA at bottom full width.
* Right sidebar (on desktop): search, contact mini form, social icons, tags.
* Footer: dark strip with copyright and small links.

## Hygraph (GraphQL) — Project setup & content models

**1. Create Hygraph project**

* Create new Hygraph project named `soundwave-samples`.
* Add CORS origins for your frontend: `http://localhost:3000`, your production URL(s).
* Generate permanent API access token for server-side admin tasks and a public token for read-only client queries.

**2. Content models** (use the exact field names below)

### Genre

* `id` (auto)
* `name` (String) — e.g. “Hip-Hop”
* `slug` (String, unique)
* `description` (RichText / String)
* `order` (Number)

### SamplePack

* `id` (auto)
* `name` (String)
* `slug` (String, unique)
* `creator` (String) — display name
* `coverArt` (Asset / Image) — Hygraph Asset
* `previewAudio` (File) — a short mp3 preview (optional)
* `genre` (Reference → Genre) — single or multiple (link packs to sub-genres)
* `subgenre` (String) — optional free text
* `description` (RichText/String)
* `downloadUrl` (String / URL) — final download link (open in new tab)
* `tags` (Tags/Text)
* `releaseDate` (Date)
* `featured` (Boolean)
* `downloadsCount` (Number) — updated server-side or via webhook
* `createdAt`, `updatedAt`

### Preset (similar structure)

* `id`
* `name`
* `slug`
* `creator`
* `coverArt` (Asset)
* `genre` (Reference → Genre)
* `pluginCompatibility` (String) — e.g., Serum, Massive
* `description`
* `downloadUrl`
* `previewAudio` (File)
* `tags`, `releaseDate`

### Plugin

* `id`, `name`, `slug`
* `developer`
* `coverArt`
* `description`
* `downloadUrl`
* `price` (Number) — optional, but site is free so keep zero or free
* `tags`, `genre`

### Tutorial

* `id`
* `name`
* `slug`
* `creator` (String) — YouTube channel name
* `youtubeId` (String) — YouTube video ID only (store ID, not raw URL)
* `videoLink` (String) — `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<ID>`
* `thumbnail` (Asset) — optional
* `genre` (Reference → Genre)
* `description` (RichText) — auto pulled or copy of YouTube description
* `publishedAt` (Date)
* `duration` (String / Number)

### Comment

* `id`
* `entityType` (Enum: `SamplePack`, `Preset`, `Plugin`, `Tutorial`)
* `entityId` (String) — store referenced entry `id` or `slug`
* `authorName` (String) — optional, allow "Anonymous"
* `text` (String)
* `createdAt`
* `isModerated` (Boolean default false)
* `ipHash` (String) — optional for spam prevention
* `likes` (Number)

> **Note:** Comments are stored as separate entries. This is easier for moderation and pagination. If you prefer, create an array field `comments` on SamplePack that references `Comment` entries.

### ContactMessage

* `id`
* `name` (String)
* `email` (String)
* `message` (String)
* `socialLinks` (JSON) — optional stored object
* `createdAt`

**3. Permissions & Roles**

* Create roles:

  * `Public` (read-only): query access to SamplePack, Preset, Plugin, Tutorial, Genre. Allow create `Comment` (with captcha/limitation) if you want public comments via API.
  * `Content Editor` (admin): full read/write to content models.
  * Use Hygraph role-based permission engine to restrict mutations to admin tokens.

**4. API tokens**

* `PUBLIC_TOKEN` — read-only, used by client.
* `ADMIN_TOKEN` (server-only) — used by serverless functions or admin UI to run mutations.

**5. Optional**: configure Hygraph Media Upload to use S3/Cloudinary, set up GraphCDN for edge caching.

## Example GraphQL queries & mutations

**Fetch featured packs + genres**

```graphql
query GetHome {
  genres(first: 20, orderBy: order_ASC) {
    id
    name
    slug
  }
  samplePacks(where: { featured: true }, first: 8) {
    id
    name
    slug
    creator
    coverArt { url }
    genre { name slug }
    description
    downloadUrl
  }
}
```

**Fetch packs by genre**

```graphql
query GetPacksByGenre($genreSlug: String!, $skip: Int = 0, $first: Int = 20) {
  genre(where: { slug: $genreSlug }) {
    id
    name
  }
  samplePacks(where: { genre: { slug: $genreSlug } }, skip: $skip, first: $first) {
    id name slug creator coverArt { url } downloadUrl description
  }
}
```

**Pack detail + comments**

```graphql
query GetPack($slug: String!) {
  samplePack(where: { slug: $slug }) {
    id name slug creator coverArt { url } downloadUrl description previewAudio { url }
    genre { name slug }
  }
  comments(where: { entityType: "SamplePack", entityId: $slug }, orderBy: createdAt_DESC) {
    id authorName text createdAt
  }
}
```

**Create comment (public mutation)**

```graphql
mutation CreateComment($data: CommentCreateInput!) {
  createComment(data: $data) {
    id text authorName createdAt
  }
}
```

`CommentCreateInput` example body:

```json
{
  "entityType": "SamplePack",
  "entityId": "mdu-hiphop-samplepack",
  "text": "This drum kit bangs!",
  "authorName": "Anonymous"
}
```

**Admin mutation example (server-side only)**

```graphql
mutation UpdateDownloads($id: ID!, $count: Int!) {
  updateSamplePack(where: { id: $id }, data: { downloadsCount: $count }) {
    id downloadsCount
  }
}
```

## Front-end architecture & implementation details

### Tech stack

* React (use Next.js if SSR/SEO desired)
* Tailwind CSS with custom theme tokens
* Apollo Client for GraphQL
* react-router (or Next.js routing)
* react-modal or headlessui dialog for modal
* react-player (for YouTube preview) OR `iframe` with sanitized `youtubeId`
* optional: Formik + Yup for contact form validation
* optional: reCAPTCHA for comment & contact spam prevention
* Optional: Vercel / Netlify for deployment

### Tailwind config (colors)

Add to `tailwind.config.js`:

### Apollo client setup

```js
// /lib/apollo.js
import { ApolloClient, InMemoryCache, HttpLink } from '@apollo/client';

const client = new ApolloClient({
  link: new HttpLink({
    uri: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_HYGRAPH_ENDPOINT,
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_HYGRAPH_TOKEN}` // read-only token
    }
  }),
  cache: new InMemoryCache()
});

export default client;
```

### PackCard example (Tailwind-driven)

* square cover image (aspect-square), name, creator, genre pills, download CTA at bottom full width
* onClick opens `PackModal` with additional info and comments

**Download button:** open `downloadUrl` in new tab:

```jsx
<button onClick={() => window.open(pack.downloadUrl, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')}>
  Download
</button>
```

### PackModal

* show `coverArt` left
* right column: name, creator, genre pills, description (truncate), comments
* comment box with placeholder “Add a comment…” and `Post` button that calls `createComment` mutation
* after posting, optimistic update to show comment, then on success clear input
* blur page background and show modal centered with `max-w-[800px]`

### Tutorial page

* Grid of tutorial cards with thumbnail, title, channel name, short description
* On click, open video frame in modal or inline player using `react-player`:

```jsx
<ReactPlayer url={`https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=${youtubeId}`} controls />
```

* Show description pulled into Hygraph `description` field.

### Contact page

* Form fields: Name, Email, Message, Social icons (optional)
* Submit hits serverless function that writes to Hygraph `ContactMessage` via admin token (or Hygraph public mutation if enabled)
* Show success toast

### Manage Content

* Nav link `Manage Content`:

  * Option A: Link directly to Hygraph admin UI (`https://app.hygraph.com/project/<id>/cms`) — simplest.
  * Option B: Build a simple admin dashboard in the app that uses ADMIN_TOKEN server-side to create/edit/delete entries. Protect this route using environment variable check & basic password (or integrate NextAuth).
* Recommend linking to Hygraph CMS UI and also building a minimal in-app editor for quick tasks.

## Comments (no sign-in) — implementation notes

* **Store comments in Hygraph** as `Comment` entries via GraphQL mutation.
* To reduce spam:

  * Rate-limit client-side creation (e.g., one per 30s).
  * Server-side (if using serverless function) validate input and optionally verify `reCAPTCHA` token.
  * Store `ipHash` or `fingerprint` (server-only) to detect duplicates.
  * Mark `isModerated` default `false`; display only comments where `isModerated` is `false` or `true` depending on moderation policy (or auto-publish and queue spam reports).
* Keep comments editable/deletable by `Content Editor` role in Hygraph.

**CreateComment mutation example (client-side using public token):**

```js
const CREATE_COMMENT = gql`
  mutation CreateComment($input: CommentCreateInput!) {
    createComment(data: $input) { id text authorName createdAt }
  }
`;
// call with entityType, entityId (slug), text, authorName
```

---

## Extra UX & accessibility suggestions

* Ensure images have `alt` attributes (coverArt alt).
* Keyboard-accessible modals (escape to close).
* Contrast ratios: test with Lighthouse / axe.
* Use `loading="lazy"` on images and audio previews.
* Use `aria-live` for comment success state.

---

## Performance & infra

* Use Hygraph + GraphCDN for edge caching.
* Serve media via a CDN (Hygraph supports asset CDNs).
* Use code-splitting and lazy loaded pages.
* Consider static generation (Next.js `getStaticProps`) for static lists with revalidation to reduce GraphQL calls.

---

## Security & privacy

* Never expose admin API token in client bundle. Use serverless functions (Vercel, Netlify functions) for server-side mutations requiring admin permissions.
* Use HTTPS only, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on external links.
* If storing user IP or fingerprint, ensure privacy disclosure in privacy policy.

---

1. Create Hygraph project, add content models (Genre, SamplePack, Preset, Plugin, Tutorial, Comment, ContactMessage).
2. Seed Hygraph with sample genres (Hip-Hop, Jazz, Lofi, Dance, Trap, Ambient).
3. Set up assets: upload a few cover images and preview audio files.
4. Create public API token and add it to `.env` (`NEXT_PUBLIC_HYGRAPH_ENDPOINT`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_HYGRAPH_TOKEN`).
5. Scaffold React app and install dependencies: `npm i @apollo/client graphql tailwindcss react-player react-modal`.
6. Implement `apollo.js` and basic queries (GetHome).
7. Build NavBar, Hero, GenrePills, PackCard, PackModal with modal + comment form wired to createComment mutation.
8. Implement `/packs` page with filters & search by name or tags.
9. Implement `/tutorials` with `react-player` embedding by stored `youtubeId`.
10. Add contact form with serverless function writing to Hygraph `ContactMessage` via admin token.
11. Add analytics & download tracking (webhook or serverless function increments `downloadsCount`).
12. Test responsiveness against the provided images: hero, pills, card grid, right sidebar, modal.
13. Deploy; configure CORS in Hygraph for your domain.

To create your **SamplePack** library in Hygraph (formerly GraphCMS) so it works perfectly with the app's GraphQL queries, follow this exact step-by-step guide.

### Step 1: Create the "Genre" Model
Since the query expects `genre { name }`, you should create a separate model for Genres so you can categorize packs efficiently.

1.  Go to the **Schema** tab (navigation bar on the left).
2.  Click **+ Add** next to "Models".
3.  **Display Name:** `Genre` | **API ID:** `Genre`.
4.  Add these fields (drag from the right sidebar):
    *   **Single Line Text:** 
        *   Display Name: `Name`
        *   Validation: Select "Required".
    *   **Slug:** 
        *   Display Name: `Slug`
        *   Template: Connect it to the `Name` field.

---

### Step 2: Create the "Sample Pack" Model
1.  Click **+ Add** next to "Models" again.
2.  **Display Name:** `Sample Pack` | **API ID:** `SamplePack`.
3.  Add the following fields in this order:

| Field Type | Display Name | API ID | Details |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Single Line Text** | `Name` | `name` | Set as **Required**. |
| **Slug** | `Slug` | `slug` | Template: `name`. Set as **Unique**. |
| **Single Line Text** | `Creator` | `creator` | e.g., "Metro Boomin" or "SoundWave". |
| **Multi Line Text** | `Description` | `description` | Set as **Required**. |
| **Asset Picker** | `Cover Art` | `coverArt` | Select **Allow multiple assets** (though we usually use one). |
| **Single Line Text** | `Download URL` | `downloadUrl` | The link to the file (Google Drive, Dropbox, etc). |
| **Boolean** | `Featured` | `featured` | Used for the "Featured Collections" on your Homepage. |
| **Reference** | `Genre` | `genre` | **Reference Type:** Two-way. **Model to reference:** `Genre`. **Multiple values?** Yes. |

---

### Step 3: Add Your Content
1.  Go to the **Content** tab (pencil icon on the far left).
2.  Select **Genre** from the dropdown.
    *   Click **+ Create Item**.
    *   Add genres like: `Lofi`, `Trap`, `Techno`, `Cinematic`.
    *   Click **Save and Publish**.
3.  Select **Sample Pack** from the dropdown.
    *   Click **+ Create Item**.
    *   Fill in the name, creator, and paste your download link.
    *   **Cover Art:** Upload a square image (1000x1000px works best).
    *   **Genre:** Click "Add existing Genre" and select one or more you created earlier.
    *   **Featured:** Toggle this ON if you want it to appear on the homepage.
    *   **IMPORTANT:** Click **Save and Publish**.

---

Your query in `services/graphqlService.ts` looks like this:

```graphql
query MyQuery {
  samplePacks {
    id
    name
    creator
    coverArt {
      url
    }
    genre {
      name
    }
    description
    downloadUrl
  }
}
```

If you followed the steps above, this query will now return:
1.  **id**: Generated automatically by Hygraph.
2.  **name**: The title of your pack.
3.  **coverArt**: An array containing the URL to your uploaded image.
4.  **genre**: An array of objects, each containing the `name` (e.g., "Trap").

---

### Step 5: API Permissions (Crucial)
If the data isn't showing up:
1.  Go to **Project Settings** -> **API Access**.
2.  Ensure your **Permanent Auth Token** has "Read" permissions for all models.
3.  Under **Public Content API**, verify that the "Defaults" allow reading published content.
